sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Wichita Falls?
sections.html:
Wichita Falls is in Wichita County. The Wichita Appraisal District values property, the City of Wichita Falls, the county and the school district set rates, and the Wichita County Tax Office collects.

The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate shows 101,951 residents, 0.3% fewer than the 2020 base and about 2.5% fewer than the 2010 count of 104,553. Owners occupy 56.4% of homes (2020 to 2024), the median owner-occupied value is $156,800, and mean travel time to work is 14.3 minutes. With values at that level, a fixed-dollar school exemption removes a large share of the typical home's school value.

The county tax office says it assesses and collects for 8 taxing jurisdictions and disbursed almost $120 million in the most recent tax year. Its 2026 rate table covers the city, the county, Wichita Falls ISD and neighboring units such as Burkburnett, Iowa Park, City View, Holliday and Electra.

  • Values, exemptions, protests: Wichita Appraisal District, P.O. Box 5172, Wichita Falls, 76307, phone (940) 322-2435, open Monday to Friday 8:00am to 5:00pm.
  • Bills and payment: Wichita County Tax Office.
  • City budget and rate hearings: the City of Wichita Falls.

sections.h2: What are the Wichita Falls tax rates for 2026?
sections.html:
The county tax office's Truth in Taxation table lists an adopted 2026 rate of $0.677900 per $100 for the City of Wichita Falls, down from $0.682500 for 2025. Wichita County adopted $0.518590 and Wichita Falls ISD adopted $1.034677.

The city's rate has two parts, $0.652925 for maintenance and operations and $0.024975 for debt. The same table gives the city's no-new-revenue rate as $0.666037 and its voter-approval rate as $0.717729. A rate above the no-new-revenue rate raises more tax from the same properties than the year before, while a rate below the voter-approval rate needs no election. The city's rate sits between the two. The school district's debt share is large next to the city's: $0.359277 of its $1.034677.

sections.h2: When is Wichita Falls property tax due?
sections.html:
The tax office posts a reminder that property taxes are due on or before January 31. Under state law, tax unpaid on February 1 is delinquent.

The statewide late schedule applies to Wichita Falls bills. A 6% penalty and 1% interest attach on February 1, the penalty gains 1% a month until it reaches 12% on July 1, and interest has no cap. A unit that has hired a collection attorney can add a penalty of up to 20%. Seniors, disabled owners and disabled veterans can pay a homestead bill in four installments, and a delinquent owner may ask about a payment plan, which some collectors extend to 36 months on a residence homestead.

  • Early spring: the appraisal district mails notices of appraised value, starting around April 1 for single-family homesteads.
  • May 15: the usual protest deadline, or 30 days after the notice is delivered if that is later.
  • July 25: the chief appraiser certifies the roll to each taxing unit.
  • October: bills go out, and tax is due on receipt.
  • January 31: the last day to pay before penalty and interest.

The tax office also notes that it follows the Wichita Falls ISD schedule for weather closures, so check before driving downtown on a bad-weather day near the deadline.

sections.h2: How do I lower a Wichita Falls property tax bill?
sections.html:
Apply for the residence homestead exemption and protest the appraisal when the value looks off. The appraisal district handles both, and exemption applications generally must be filed before May 1.

The state requires a school district exemption of $140,000 on a residence homestead and an additional $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled. The county tax office's exemption page, quoting the Comptroller, adds that exemptions need an application in most cases and that the chief appraiser decides whether property qualifies. Counties, cities and colleges may adopt their own percentage or dollar exemptions, so ask the appraisal district what the city and county have adopted.

  • Disabled veteran exemptions run from $5,000 for a rating of 10% to 29% up to $12,000 for 70% to 100%, and a veteran rated 100% disabled can receive a total exemption on a residence homestead.
  • A homestead appraisal cannot rise more than 10% a year once the exemption has been granted for a year.
  • Owners 65 or older or disabled can freeze the school district tax on their home.
  • A surviving spouse age 55 or older may keep a deceased spouse's over-65 benefits in certain cases.

After a protest, an owner who still disagrees with the appraisal review board can go to district court or use regular binding arbitration. For a board value above $1,000,000 the State Office of Administrative Hearings is an option. Any appeal still requires paying at least the undisputed tax before the delinquency date.

sections.h2: What does the Wichita Falls tax rate trend look like?
sections.html:
The city's rate has drifted down over five years. The county's table lists $0.694321 for 2022, $0.680000 for 2023, $0.684800 for 2024, $0.682500 for 2025 and $0.677900 for 2026.

Wichita Falls ISD fell faster in the same table, from $1.296500 in 2022 to $1.034677 in 2026, and Wichita County slid from $0.560400 to $0.518590. Since all three rates moved down while the city's population was flat, any increase in a homeowner's bill comes from a higher taxable value, not a higher rate. The homestead cap limits that increase to 10% a year on the appraised value of a qualifying home, and it applies only to homesteads.

That is worth checking before a sale. If a notice of appraised value jumped by more than the cap allows, ask the appraisal district at (940) 322-2435 whether the homestead exemption is on file. A missing exemption would leave the full school value on the bill.

sections.h2: What happens to Wichita Falls property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The lien attaches on January 1, so the current year's tax is settled at closing from the seller's proceeds. A buyer cannot get clear title while delinquent tax is outstanding on the account.

The person who owned the property on January 1 is liable for that year's tax, even if the house sells in March. Ask the county tax office for a statement covering each unit before you list. Inherited homes follow the same rules, and heirs not named on a recorded deed supply an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim a homestead exemption. A buyer who acquires after January 1 can get the exemption for the rest of the year if the prior owner never received it.

If taxes are delinquent, the collector sends notices, may offer a payment plan, and can sue. Court costs are added to the bill. Tax foreclosure sales are auctions run by the constable or an agent hired by the unit, and Texas gives former owners a limited right to redeem, with a longer window for homestead, agricultural and mineral property.

faqs.q: What is the Wichita Falls city tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: $0.677900 per $100 of taxable value, listed as adopted in the Wichita County Tax Office's Truth in Taxation table. It was $0.682500 for tax year 2025.

faqs.q: When are Wichita County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1. The tax office says taxes are due before or on January 31, and unpaid tax on February 1 carries a 6% penalty plus 1% interest, with the penalty rising monthly to 12% in July.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Wichita Falls appraisal?
faqs.a: Call the Wichita Appraisal District at (940) 322-2435 or write to cs@wadtx.com. The district is open Monday to Friday, 8:00am to 5:00pm.

faqs.q: How many taxing units does the Wichita County Tax Office collect for?
faqs.a: The tax office says it assesses and collects for 8 taxing jurisdictions and disbursed almost $120 million in its most recent tax year.

faqs.q: Does Wichita Falls have a lower tax rate than last year?
faqs.a: Yes, for the city, county and school district. The adopted rates in the county's table fell from 0.682500 to 0.677900 for the city and from 1.075287 to 1.034677 for Wichita Falls ISD.
